definition: Keeping tokens whose probability is at least a fraction of the top token's probability.
details: Keeping tokens whose probability is at least a fraction of the top token's probability. Scales the cutoff with confidence and behaves better than top-p at high temperatures; popular in open-model serving.

explainer.lead: Min-p sampling keeps tokens whose probability is at least a fraction of the top token's probability. It matters because it scales the cutoff with model confidence and behaves better than top-p at high temperatures, which is why it is popular in open-model serving.

tiers.eli5: When a model picks its next word, it ignores any option far less likely than the best one — how far depends on how sure it is.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use min-p as a decoding filter in open-model serving, setting the fraction threshold that defines the cutoff. A pitfall is tuning as if it were top-p: min-p's scaled cutoff and high-temperature behaviour differ.
tiers.paperLevel: Min-p sampling retains tokens whose probability is at least a fraction of the top token's probability; the cutoff scales with confidence, and it is reported to behave better than top-p at high temperatures.

explainer.example: With a fraction of 0.1 and a top token probability of 0.6, any token below 0.06 is dropped before sampling.
